newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP cites currency rise/price falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP cites currency rise/price falls.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday that the fall in its first quarter earnings was partly due to a higher Australian dollar and lower prices for copper and steel products.
Of its four key divisions, only the petroleum group increased after tax profit in the three mnths ended August 31.

Petroleum earnings rose by 204.8 percent to A$189 million while the copper division suffered the largest fall with a 55.5 percent decline to A$85 million, minerals fell 39.7 percent to A$76 million and the steel division dropped 38.4 percent to A$90 million.
The service companies group increased after tax profit by 233.3 percent to A$20 million.

BHP, Australia's largest company in terms of market capitalisation and one of the best known among international investors, said first quarter net profit fell 22.8 percent to A$287.0 million. Operating profit fell 23.8 percent to A$586.0 million, while sales rose 2.7 percent to A$4.84 billion.

The lower result from the copper division, which includes the Magma Copper operations acquired earlier this year, was due to "lower realised copper prices and disappointing results from the North American operations".

The fall in steel division earnings was due to lower results from the flat products and long products division which was affected by lower average export prices and lower Austalian domestic despatches.
It said the division benefitted to some extent from the inclusion of Tubemakers' results.

Generally, the company said its first quarter result was affected by "the adverse impact of the higher A$/US$ exchange rate which averaged 79 cents compared with 73 cents for the corresponding period".
BHP said the minerals division result included a A$45 million loss from the sale of the Mali gold assets.

The petroleum division, whose profits were coming off a low base of A$62 million a year ago, included a net profit of A$50 million from the sale of BHP's share in the Mungo/Monan development in the United Kingdom, higher crude oil and natural gas prices, increased refining margins, and lower depreciation with the write-off of Dai Hung field in Vietnam in May 2996.
The company's statement did not contain any commentary about the outlook for the remainder of the financial year.
